summary: KEP-1027 proposes standardized union (oneOf) semantics for Kubernetes API types...
rationale: Union semantics are implicit in core types...
note: Accurately reflects its long-standing "implementable" but incomplete status and reliance on Server-Side Apply.

summary: KEP-378 (Kubernetes Bootstrap Checkpointing) proposed checkpointing annotated control-plane pods...
rationale: The design goal was to record annotated Pods to the filesystem...
note: Correctly captures the retroactive status assignment and bypassed PRR during the 2021 KEP cleanup.

summary: KEP-2377 proposed a declarative kustomize format to expose imperative kubectl transformation...
rationale: Gaps in kubectl force users to write scripts...
note: Correctly identifies the original Kustomize KEP and its replacement by KEP-2386.

summary: KEP-2263 proposes a plan for testing the scalability and performance of Kubernetes storage...
rationale: The KEP addresses the lack of known scale limits and SLOs...
note: Correctly describes the scalability testing goals and the ongoing/implementable nature of the test plan.

summary: KEP-2129 proposed deprecating and removing cAdvisor v1 JSON metrics...
rationale: cAdvisor only supports Linux and a small set of runtimes...
note: Accurately details the rationale for removing cAdvisor v1 JSON endpoints to reduce double-collection costs.

summary: KEP-1435 proposed relaxing Kubernetes API validation so that a type=LoadBalancer Service can declare ports...
rationale: Users wanted one IP address exposing multiple L4 protocols...
note: Correctly identifies the relaxation of API validation for mixed L4 protocols on LoadBalancers.

summary: KEP-980 adds a service.kubernetes.io/load-balancer-cleanup finalizer to Services...
rationale: Service controller can leave orphaned load balancer resources...
note: Accurately describes the finalizer added to prevent orphaned cloud load balancers upon service deletion.

summary: KEP-5030 proposes making cluster-autoscaler aware of CSI volume attach limits...
rationale: Cluster-autoscaler ignores CSI attach limits for upcoming nodes...
note: Accurately captures the decoupling of CA simulation and scheduler behaviors for CSI volume limits.

summary: KEP-789 proposed removing the system:unauthenticated subject from the default system:discovery...
rationale: The CVE-2018-1002105 post-mortem and privacy concerns...
note: Correctly links the RBAC default bindings hardening to the CVE-2018-1002105 post-mortem.

summary: KEP-5589 proposes removing Kubernetes' runtime and generation-time dependencies on the unmaintained gogo...
rationale: Gogo protobuf has been unmaintained since 2021...
note: Accurately describes the rationale and dependency removal strategy for the unmaintained gogo protobuf library.

summary: KEP-3614 proposes that kubeadm start adding new etcd members as learners...
rationale: Members added as voting members can disrupt cluster quorum...
note: Accurately details the etcd learner mode feature gate and correctly notes the conflicting provisional/beta metadata.

summary: KEP-495 added an opt-in pod-level `ShareProcessNamespace` boolean...
rationale: The design addresses the lack of PID namespace sharing...
note: Correctly tracks the lifecycle of `ShareProcessNamespace` up to its feature gate removal in v1.19.

summary: KEP-491 covers kubectl diff, which shows how applying a configuration would change...
rationale: The feature let users see how configuration changes would affect the cluster...
note: Accurately identifies this as a retroactive KEP for a feature that was implemented prior to the KEP process.

summary: KEP-902 adds an optional Preempting (PreemptionPolicy) field to PriorityClass..."
rationale: Batch workloads with backlogs of unscheduled pods could have partially completed work discarded...
note: Correctly identifies the GA milestone (1.24) and the rationale protecting batch workloads from preemption.

summary: KEP-2053 exposes hugepage requests and limits (all page sizes) through the downward API...
rationale: Pods could not read their hugepage request or limits via the downward API...
note: Accurately details the extension of the downward API to include hugepages.

summary: KEP-2221 proposed deprecating and then removing dockershim...
rationale: Dockershim ran inside kubelet and was tightly coupled to its lifecycle...
note: Accurately captures the highly publicized removal of dockershim in Kubernetes v1.24.

summary: KEP-4580 proposed deprecating kubelet RunOnce mode...
rationale: RunOnce mode does not work in systemd mode...
outcome_reason: The provisional status is the recorded fact...
note: Accurately tracks the missed code freeze and eventual abandonment of the KEP by its author.

summary: KEP-5732 adds topology-aware and DRA-aware workload scheduling...
rationale: The problem is that the default pod-centric scheduler cannot resolve group-level topology constraints...
note: Correctly captures the newer architectural developments in PodGroup placements and DRA integration.

summary: KEP-383 graduates the new Event API (events.k8s.io/v1) to GA...
rationale: Existing Events are spammy, have unclear semantics...
note: Correctly tracks the graduation and deduplication mechanisms of the events.k8s.io/v1 API.

summary: KEP-5295 proposes KYAML, a strict subset ("dialect") of YAML...
rationale: Conventional block-style YAML is whitespace-sensitive and has type-coercion traps...
note: Accurately describes the KYAML strict-YAML subset initiative to prevent type-coercion traps.

summary: KEP-281 (Dynamic Kubelet Configuration) was deprecated in v1.22...
rationale: The feature had been stuck in alpha for years because maintainers did not push it to beta...
outcome_reason: The sources say the feature was deprecated because of lack of interest...
note: Correctly states the feature was deprecated in v1.22 due to lack of promotion interest and later withdrawn.

summary: KEP-600 proposed letting the advanced audit configuration be changed dynamically...
rationale: The motivation was that advanced audit configuration is hard to get right...
outcome_reason: The sources do not state why the KEP was withdrawn on 2021-05-05...
note: Accurately reflects the withdrawal due to stalled progress and lack of roadmap consensus.

summary: KEP-2718 proposed a client exec proxy extension to Kubernetes client libraries...
rationale: Existing client auth mechanisms cannot easily sign whole requests...
note: Accurately describes the API structure disagreements that led to its withdrawal at the alpha stage.

summary: KEP-4706 proposed deprecating kustomize in kubectl...
rationale: The KEP argued that kubectl should not promote one customization tool over others...
outcome_reason: The sources state the decision was to not pursue the removal...
note: Correctly captures the SIG Architecture decision to reject Kustomize removal due to the risk of user disruption.

summary: KEP-3156 proposed adding HTTP/3 support to the kube-apiserver..."
rationale: HTTP/3 was expected to fix head-of-line blocking...
outcome_reason: Deferred until HTTP/3 is supported by the Golang standard library...
note: Correctly identifies the hard dependency on the Go standard library for HTTP/3 support implementation.

summary: KEP-3130 proposed adding a kube-apiserver-generated transaction UID...
rationale: Correlating a kube-apiserver->kms-plugin->KMS envelope operation today relies on approximate timestamps...
outcome_reason: The sources do not give a detailed reason for the replacement...
note: Accurately tracks its subsumption and replacement by KEP-3299 (KMS v2 Improvements).

summary: KEP-4153 proposed declaring Kubernetes native API validation rules via IDL tags...
rationale: Hand-written validation is hard for users to access, review, maintain...
outcome_reason: The sources do not say why the KEP was replaced...
note: Correctly identifies the shift to declarative validation tags and its eventual replaced status.

summary: KEP-2451 proposed a ServiceAccountToken volume projection so pods receive a service account token...
rationale: The KEP addressed the security and scalability problems of storing service account tokens as secrets...
outcome_reason: The sources say it was replaced by KEP-1205 Bound Service Account Tokens...
note: Accurately identifies this design as being replaced by KEP-1205.

summary: KEP-1205 Bound Service Account Tokens proposed an API for workloads to request audience-, time- and eventually key-bound JSON Web Tokens...
rationale: The existing service account token mechanism did not meet sig-auth's security and scalability requirements...
note: Correctly identifies this KEP as the implemented successor to KEP-2451.

summary: KEP-753 introduces sidecar containers as init containers with restartPolicy: Always...
rationale: Sidecars were hard to model: they need to start before regular containers...
note: Accurately describes the `restartPolicy: Always` mechanism used to solve the init container lifecycle problem.

summary: KEP-1287 proposed allowing Pod resource requests and limits to be updated in place...
rationale: Changing container resources previously required recreating the Pod...
note: Accurately describes making PodSpec resources mutable to avoid restart penalties for batch workloads.

summary: KEP-2400 proposed basic Linux node swap support...
rationale: Kubernetes did not support swap on Linux because it is hard to guarantee and account for pod memory...
note: Correctly captures the controlled introduction and behaviors of basic Linux swap support.

summary: KEP-127 adds a hostUsers field to pod spec so pods can run in their own Linux user namespace...
rationale: Running container processes as root inside the container is a major risk...
note: Accurately describes the security motivation and mechanism of mapping container root to unprivileged host IDs.

summary: KEP-277 adds Ephemeral Containers: a temporary container added to an already-running pod...
rationale: Debugging running pods required binaries that were not in the pod image...
note: Accurately captures the `kubectl debug` workflow implementation and limitations placed on the ephemeral containers.

summary: KEP-1040 replaces the existing max-in-flight request handler in the apiserver with Priority and Fairness...
rationale: The existing max-in-flight limits (mutating and readonly only) cannot stop one category of requests from crowding out others...
note: Correctly outlines the queueing and priority level mechanics to protect the API Server from overload.
